articles.title: As electric two-wheelers gain a foothold, Belgian startup Any bets on cargo space
articles.summary: Launched by Belgian startup Any, LUV1 is a modular electric motorcycle with 120 liters of cargo space that can be used to carry bags, work equipment, or even pets.

articles.title: AI, athletes, and Keith Rabois: StrictlyVC is back in New York on September 10
articles.summary: A boutique StrictlyVC evening returns to New York's West Village on September 10 with Keith Rabois, Craig Shapiro, Jason Levien, Tristan Walker, Brynn Putnam, and Deven Parekh — covering AI, sports investing, community-building, venture economics, and politics, with cocktails, food, and networking throughout the night.

articles.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are joining the AI stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
articles.summary: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, the AI Stage is back to dig into the single hottest topic in the community for the past few years, presented by Google for Startups.

articles.title: Rivian’s CFO is leaving the company
articles.summary: Claire McDonough is stepping down on October 30 to pursue a new opportunity, the company said in a filing on Thursday.

articles.title: Bluesky adds an ‘algorithmic opt-out’ feature for those who don’t want to go viral
articles.summary: Sometimes people just want to post to their followers, Bluesky says.

articles.title: Buried in Meta’s $18B settlement is a legal pass on kids’ data
articles.summary: Meta’s settlement with 29 states allows it to retain certain data from children under 13 to train and test age-detection models, highlighting a privacy trade-off built into the deal.

articles.title: YouTube now lets creators tag Amazon products and earn commissions from purchases
articles.summary: The update turns product recommendations into a more direct revenue stream for creators, and for Amazon, the move puts its massive online marketplace inside one of the most popular video platforms.

articles.title: Barret Zoph, the Thinking Machines co-founder ousted before joining OpenAI, is now at Google
articles.summary: Zoph, who co-founded Thinking Machines Lab alongside Mira Murati and also served as the startup's CTO, led a brief stint at OpenAI and is now at Google.

articles.title: ATF declares ‘major incident’ as ransomware gang claims hack
articles.summary: The ATF is the latest federal government agency in recent years to notify Congress of a "major incident" involving its cybersecurity.

articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
articles.summary: Some of the world's largest tech companies and AI startups have come together to decry the current state of cybersecurity and to advertise a new solution that they say can ward off a new generation of cyber threats.

articles.title: Google’s new Fitbit Air brings Pokémon Sleep to your wrist
articles.summary: Google teamed up with the Pokémon Company to introduce a special-edition Fitbit Air that works with the Pokémon Sleep app.

articles.title: Fashion startup Atorie raises $9.5M to bring consumers luxury goods without the markup
articles.summary: Shoppers can visit the Atorie website and buy handbags or clothes made from the same material — and coming from the same factory — that manufacturers use in high-end goods.

articles.title: Hoomanely’s building a smart feeding bowl and an AI platform to help owners spot when their pup is sick
articles.summary: Hoomanely has developed a smart bowl to measure and record dogs' feeding data, then tells owners if behaviors change.

articles.title: Google’s AI Mode can now track flight prices, help book hotels, and more
articles.summary: The updates indicate that Google is looking to position AI Mode as an AI travel agent of sorts, as it's moving beyond simply helping users find information to actually handling parts of the trip-planning and booking process.

articles.title: This former PG&E engineer is building a ‘Google Maps for the underground’
articles.summary: The startup just raised a $26 million Series A to grow its customer base and help reduce red tape for utility and construction work.

articles.title: Hugging Face is selling a cute $399 open source duck robot, Microduck
articles.summary: Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said the Microduck is an “open-source robot you can teach new tricks with reinforcement learning.”

articles.title: Hold up, there’s a new Twitter in town
articles.summary: Former Twitter trademark counsel Stephen Coates said in a LinkedIn post that the company is not trying to re-create Twitter.

articles.title: Sprains, pain, and whiplash: Waymo and Zoox test drivers are getting hurt as robotaxis scale
articles.summary: Test drivers for Waymo and Zoox sustained more than two dozen injuries in 2024 and 2025 from hard braking or other sudden movements made by the autonomous vehicles, according to a TechCrunch review of data submitted to OSHA.

articles.title: Australian police arrest two over TeamPCP hacks targeting Mercor, OpenAI, and others
articles.summary: The arrests come after a wave of cyberattacks earlier this year targeting tech companies that rely on high-profile and widely used open source software.

articles.title: AI’s memory crunch is coming for Android apps
articles.summary: Google is setting new memory-use limits for Android apps as AI data centers contribute to hardware shortages that could leave lower-cost phones with less memory.
